verses.text: But there were also false prophets among God's people long ago, and there will be false teachers among you. They will secretly bring in teachings that destroy people. They will even reject the Master who paid to set them free, and they will quickly bring destruction on themselves.
Many people will follow their sexual sins, and because of them, people will speak badly about the way of truth.
Because they are greedy, these teachers will use made-up stories to take money from you. But God's judgment on them was decided long ago, and it is not asleep. Their destruction is coming.
God did not spare the angels who sinned. He threw them down to the deepest pit, and put them in chains of darkness, to be kept there until the judgment.
He did not spare the ancient world, but he sent a flood on the people who did not care about him. Yet he protected Noah, who preached about doing right, and seven others with him.
God condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah and burned them to ashes. He made them an example of what will happen to people who do not care about him.
But he rescued Lot, a good man, who was very upset by the shameful lives of those evil people.
That good man lived among them, and day after day the evil things he saw and heard hurt his good heart.
So the Lord knows how to rescue those who honour him from their troubles. And he knows how to keep evil people under punishment until the day of judgment.
This is especially true of those who follow the dirty desires of their bodies and look down on authority. They are proud and stubborn, and they are not afraid to insult glorious beings in heaven.
Even angels, who are much stronger and more powerful, do not bring insulting charges against such beings before the Lord.
But these people are like animals without reason, born only to be caught and killed. They insult what they do not understand, and they will be destroyed like animals.

They will be paid back with harm for the harm they have done. They enjoy wild partying in broad daylight. They are like dirty spots and stains among you, enjoying their tricks while they eat with you.
Their eyes are always looking for someone to sleep with, and they never stop sinning. They trap people who are weak in faith. Their hearts are trained in greed. They are under God's curse!
They have left the right road and wandered off. They followed the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the money he could get by doing wrong.
But Balaam was told off for his wrong. A donkey, which cannot talk, spoke with a human voice and stopped the prophet's madness.
These people are like springs with no water, and like clouds blown by a storm. The deepest darkness is waiting for them forever.
They boast with big, empty words. They use sexual desires to trap people who have only just escaped from those who live wrong lives.
They promise them freedom, but they themselves are slaves to what destroys them. People are slaves to whatever controls them.
They had escaped the dirt of the world by knowing our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. If they get caught up in it again and are beaten by it, they end up worse than they were at the beginning.
It would have been better for them never to have known the right way, than to know it and then turn away from the holy command they were given.
What happened to them shows that these true sayings are right: "A dog goes back to its vomit," and "A pig that is washed goes back to roll in the mud."
